top_story: The UAE’s decision to quit OPEC on May 1 marks a significant Gulf realignment, sharpening questions about how Abu Dhabi is redefining its autonomy as regional wars reorder alliances and energy politics. That shift lands alongside scrutiny of Dubai as a refuge for Sudan’s RSF leadership, whose reported property holdings underscore how Gulf financial space can insulate armed actors accused of mass atrocities while Sudan’s war devastates civilians. Wendy Sherman’s charge that Benjamin Netanyahu led Washington into a genocidal course in Gaza reflects how the war has moved from battlefield crisis to a broader rupture in U.S.-regional relations and political legitimacy. Taken together, these developments show a Middle East in which conflict is not only redrawing front lines but also reshaping Gulf power centers, external partnerships, and the structures that shield or sustain violence.
